facts.text: Shepard's Golf Balls was deployed at Fra Mauro during Apollo 14 in 1971.

Alan Shepard attached a 6-iron head to a sample tool handle and hit two golf balls on live TV, famously claiming one went 'miles and miles.' Analysis later estimated about 40 yards. The balls are still out there.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the lunar environment.

Provided a memorable demonstration of reduced lunar gravity — a ball hit one-handed in a bulky spacesuit traveled roughly 40 yards in one-sixth gravity, six times farther than the same swing would achieve on Earth.
Status: Remains preserved in the arid regolith at Fra Mauro.
The two golf balls remain on the surface at Fra Mauro; the makeshift 6-iron club head is on display at the USGA Golf Museum in Far Hills, New Jersey.
